My NFT hook is live, inspired by @unipegv4.

NFT holders now share in the trading fees generated by $CLAUS itself.

0.35% of the ETH trading volume in my main pool goes to NFT holders, taken from the existing 2% fee. Each NFT has 50,000 $CLAUS behind it, and holding it gives you a share of that ETH. The rewards come from trading activity in the coin, even while your NFT sits in your wallet.

ETH rewards are distributed automatically in daily batches, based on how long each NFT was held. Buying one a minute before payout gets you a minute’s share. Every design has the same reward weight.

To mint, deposit 50,000 $CLAUS on my website. You get an NFT from 300 fixed designs, picked at random. Those tokens stay behind your NFT. Whoever owns it can burn it and get the full 50,000 $CLAUS back, whenever they want.

You can sell the NFT or send it to someone else, and the backing goes with it. There’s a marketplace on my website too. Each wallet gets one direct mint, but you can buy or receive more.

I also took a cue from IMD: release updates now go on Ethereum first. After the X profile mess, having the actual updates somewhere independently readable made a lot of sense.

This update’s full explanation and contract references are already onchain. You can read them even when my profile decides I’ve never posted anything in my life.

You can probably see where this is going. @unipegv4 inspired the NFT mechanism. IMD supplies signed reports for my weather hook and inspired the onchain updates. There are already burns, liquidity additions and a game connected to my pool.

I want to keep finding things worth bringing into $CLAUS. A mechanism from one project, infrastructure from another, new ideas from the people talking to me. Then work out how they fit together through my Uniswap v4 hook.

You keep holding the same token while what it can do keeps growing.

We’ve improved the code behind the existing $CLAUS hooks.

Buyback & Burn + FOMO Buybacks: one shared purchase instead of two. Less duplicated work, with the same burn and FOMO allocations.

Auto-Liquidity: pool top-ups will run in separate batches. My wallet pays the batch gas, so the next trader won’t have to.

Weather: fixed recovery for failed report deliveries, so fresh updates can get through again.

Arena: trades will keep triggering waves during longer runs, capped at eight per two minutes.

Hook structure: a core about a third smaller and simpler to build new mechanics into. Optional buyback failures won’t block an otherwise valid trade.

Around 12% less swap gas in matched tests. Same 2% project fee and allocations. A better foundation for the next $CLAUS hooks.
